messages:
tara: getting an incoming escalation from CS — multiple eu-west customers reporting SSE streams that cut out mid-response and a few cases of duplicated final token batches (apparently billed twice). Started around 10:12 UTC.

nikhil: seeing spikes on w-gw-eu-01 upstream errors and nginx 502s on streaming gateway. synthetic monitors show 20% of streams terminated with status 502/524.

fiona: I pulled gateway logs and theres a flurry of TLS errors during renegotiation: 
```
2026-04-02T10:11:58.482Z stream-router[warn] tls: unexpected renegotiation from client session id=0x9f2b
2026-04-02T10:12:03.103Z nginx[err] 502 while reading upstream, client=1.2.3.4, upstream=10.0.1.12:443, context=streaming
2026-04-02T10:12:03.104Z gw[euw01][info] connection=xyz789 closed abnormally, active_clients=743
```

jess: Any recent deploys? I know we rolled out stream-router v1.5.3 to canary eu-west this morning. Could be a protocol mismatch with the newer keepalive/ssl settings.

nikhil: Confirmed: canary rollout of stream-router v1.5.3 at 09:50 UTC. The new router sends a ServerHello with TLS1.3 post-handshake that some older client stacks (esp older mobile SDKs and corporate proxies) choke on, causing abrupt closes. When clients reconnect they sometimes request the tail of the stream which the fanout service re-emits, leading to duplicate token deliveries and two billing records before dedupe triggers.

tara: CS notes indicate duplicated charges in 6 customers so far. We need immediate mitigation and a status update.

fiona: Hot mitigations I'm initiating: 1) pause canary and rollback stream-router to v1.5.2 in eu-west; 2) reduce nginx keepalive_timeout from 65s->15s to avoid long-lived half-closed connections behind proxies; 3) temporary server-side dedupe window of 45s at billing write path.

deploy-bot: Rollback requested by fiona for service=stream-router region=eu-west request=rb-2026-04-02-01

jess: I'll coordinate rollback. Also enabling stricter TLS policy to disable post-handshake renegotiation in the canary path.

nikhil: Reproducer for CS and devs (non-destructive):
```
# open SSE, then force TLS renegotiation via openssl s_client while stream is active
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/chat?model=redwood-chat-medium &
# from another shell:
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -no_ign_eof -ign_eof -status \
  -servername api.redwood.ai -tls1_3 -quiet \n# drop the s_client after a few seconds to mimic proxies dropping the renegotiation
```
Notes: older Node and Android HTTP libraries can reset on unexpected TLS events which truncates the current chunk. If the router had buffered a partial chunk, fanout may deliver it on reconnect as a new event.

fiona: kernel/net changes applied on w-gw-eu-01..04: net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=60, net.ipv4.tcp_fin_timeout=20. Also cycled nginx workers to pick up keepalive change. Watching connection closure rates.

nikhil: billing hotfix: added a 45s dedupe window keyed by parent_request_id + batch_seq in eu-west write path; flagged behind feature gate until we validate behavior. Pushing to canary now.

support-bot: Drafting status page update: 
- Status: partial outage (degraded streaming) 
- Impact: eu-west streaming clients may experience truncated streams and rare duplicate billing events 
- Mitigation: rolled back stream-router canary, enforced stricter TLS policy, nginx keepalive reduced, billing dedupe enabled in canary 
Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-452

tara: CS: please provide the curl/openssl repro to affected customers so they can verify. Also request refunds for duplicate invoices and open billing investigations for the six impacted accounts.

jess: Canary rollback completed at 10:27 UTC; stream-router back to v1.5.2 across eu-west. Monitoring shows error-rate dropped from 18%->1.6% in 5m.

nikhil: Early validation: two affected customers confirmed no further duplicates after dedupe and rollback. FD/socket counts normalized.

fiona: Preliminary RCA: stream-router v1.5.3 introduced post-handshake TLS behavior that triggered resets in some client/proxy stacks. Those abrupt closes caused partial chunk emission on reconnect that the fanout + billing pipeline counted as new batches before dedupe. Contributing factor: long nginx keepalive allowed half-closed sockets to linger behind proxies.

tara: Action items: 1) jess/nikhil to add a canary test covering TLS post-handshake compatibility and add a blocker on post-handshake renegotiation until client compatibility is validated; 2) lucas (billing team) to make dedupe permanent and extend logs for any skipped batches; 3) fiona to add automated alerts for TLS-error spikes and nginx keepalive saturation.

support-bot: Pagerduty incident created PD-99221.

jess: Assigning postmortem to nikhil, due 72h. I'll own the customer comms template with tara.

tara: Thanks everyone. I'll send the status update and coordinate refunds. Keep this thread for progress and paste any follow-ups here.
